profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for a journal revision and accompanying code release of a paper on Programmable Actor Reinforcement Learning (PARL) for inventory management. The team has three weeks before sending the revised manuscript to Operations Research and wants to lock down what experiments need to be rerun, what counts as a successful reproduction of the reported results, and what should be included in the first public release of the modular Python library. The agenda is to divide responsibilities for experiment reruns, finalize the reproduction package scope, and set a timeline for code freeze, figures, and release notes. The expected outcome is a concrete work plan covering experiment execution, artifact packaging, and deadlines.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Reinforcement learning for operations management, approximate dynamic programming, inventory control
members.background: Maya led the original PARL paper and designed most of the experimental framing, including the inventory network benchmarks and comparisons to heuristics and RL baselines.
members.private_state: She wants a clean journal resubmission with minimal disruption to the already-written narrative, and she is trying to avoid opening up a large engineering effort that could delay the revision.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the paper environment,' they mean the archived experiment branch used to generate the submitted results, not the latest cleaned-up simulator branch.
Rerunning baselines means executing the published baselines with the same hyperparameters and adding a few fresh random seeds for stability, not doing a new tuning campaign.
If the main constrained settings show the same ranking and broadly similar average gains, that is enough to say the table is reproduced for revision purposes.
A first library release can be a research artifact: code, configs, and one working example are sufficient even if packaging and docs are light.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: ML experiment infrastructure, reproducibility tooling, mathematical programming integration, Python packaging
members.background: Leo joined the lab after the initial submission and has been refactoring the inventory simulator, solver wrappers, and experiment launcher to prepare for broader reuse.
members.private_state: He wants to use the revision window to put the project on solid reproducibility footing and avoid releasing something brittle that will create maintenance debt later.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to 'the paper environment,' they mean the current canonical simulator branch with bug fixes and standardized config handling, because that is what should back any public artifact.
Rerunning baselines means giving each baseline a fair fresh sweep under the same compute budget and current harness, otherwise the comparison is not really reproducible.
Reproducing the main table means regenerating every reported row from scratch on a fresh setup with the current pipeline, not just matching the headline trend on the hardest cases.
A library release should be installable and self-contained enough that an external researcher can run multiple benchmark structures without lab-specific setup.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to rerun experiments in 'the paper environment.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the archived branch `camera_ready_mar12` that produced the submission figures, including the old simulator behavior and solver wrapper.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the current `main` branch after the February demand-truncation fix and the refactored lead-time handling, because that is now the canonical implementation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both branches are internally associated with the paper, and saying 'paper environment' sounds specific enough that neither expects ambiguity; the divergence sits in version identity rather than an obvious design choice.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they should 'rerun the baselines for fairness.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means rerunning PPO, A3C, and the heuristic policies with the originally reported hyperparameters and 5 new seeds to verify stability.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means re-tuning each baseline in the current launcher on each topology with the same compute budget used for PARL, then running the selected settings across seeds.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML research, 'rerun' often informally covers both replaying and re-searching settings, and fairness language makes the phrase feel mutually understood even though the operational workload is very different.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'reproduce the main table'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to 'reproduce the main table before the revision goes out.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks reproduction is achieved if the constrained-settings summary still shows PARL ahead by roughly the same margin and the qualitative ranking of methods is unchanged.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks reproduction is achieved only if every row in the main results table can be regenerated end-to-end with comparable means and variance bars from the refreshed pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They share the same goal phrase and both care about credibility, but 'reproduce' hides different stopping rules; neither side feels the need to unpack the acceptance threshold in a short planning discussion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss getting 'the library release' ready alongside the revision.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the release includes the PARL code, benchmark configs for the paper, and one example notebook for a single-echelon inventory problem.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the release includes an installable package, benchmark registry for multiple supply-chain structures, solver backend instructions, and enough documentation for outside users to run experiments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view these items as part of a library, but they differ on boundary conditions between a minimal artifact and a general-purpose release; because they are speaking cooperatively about 'getting it out,' the scope gap remains implicit.

If we can reproduce the main table in the constrained settings where PARL looked strongest, and the averages still tell the same story, that's enough for the revision. The library release should be lightweight: the paper code, configs, and one example so we can point reviewers to an artifact without creating a giant side project.
